source.quote: New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it

requirements.exclusion: Whether an implementation is new is not in any message: a session using the feature is equally consistent with an existing implementation that has not yet migrated, which the sentence asks only to migrate.

source.quote: existing implementations SHOULD migrate to integrating directly with LLM provider APIs.

requirements.exclusion: Asks for a migration over time, which one recording cannot show either way — a session that uses the feature may come from an implementation partway through migrating, and the feature remains in the specification until removal.

source.quote: For trust & safety and security, there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny sampling requests.

requirements.exclusion: Policy and UI: whether a human reviews sampling requests, and whether they can deny one, is the client application's design. A request answered with a result may have been approved by a person or by policy; nothing in the answer says which.

source.quote: Applications SHOULD: Provide UI that makes it easy and intuitive to review sampling requests; Allow users to view and edit prompts before sending; Present generated responses for review before delivery

requirements.exclusion: Binds the client's user interface — what it shows the user, offers them, or lets them do — and none of that reaches the wire: a recording carries the client's messages, not its screens. The reference host this project ships has no interactive interface at all (it answers from its interaction script, `crates/mcp-reference-host/src/handler.rs`), so the clause is a host-implementation property, reviewed in the host, never judged from a trace.

source.quote: Clients MUST declare support for tool use via the `sampling.tools` capability to receive tool-enabled sampling requests.

requirements.exclusion: The precondition half of the sentence. A client that has not declared `sampling.tools` does nothing wrong by receiving a tool-enabled request — the server does, and the sentence's other half (`sampling.tools-declared`) judges it. Nothing the client sends can break this half: the declaration is either made or not, and its absence becomes a violation only when such a request arrives, which is the server's act.

source.quote: Servers MUST NOT send tool-enabled sampling requests to Clients that have not declared support for tool use via the `sampling.tools` capability.
Clients that support sampling MUST declare the `sampling` capability in `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` on each request:
Servers SHOULD avoid using these values (e.g. can just omit `includeContext` since it defaults to `"none"`)
and SHOULD NOT use them unless the client declares `sampling.context` capability.
When a user message contains tool results (type: "tool_result"), it MUST contain ONLY tool results.

When using tool use in sampling, every assistant message containing `ToolUseContent` blocks MUST be followed by a user message that consists entirely of `ToolResultContent` blocks, with each tool use (e.g. with `id: $id`) matched by a corresponding tool result (with `toolUseId: $id`), before any other message.
`{mode: "required"}`: Model MUST use at least one tool before completing
`{mode: "none"}`: Model MUST NOT use any tools
Sampling messages MUST contain a `role` field of `"user"` or `"assistant"`; and a `content` field representing the message data.
The list of messages in a sampling request SHOULD NOT be retained between separate requests.

requirements.exclusion: Retention is client-internal state: the next request's `messages` are the server's, and say nothing about what the client kept from the last one.

source.quote: The client MUST respect the `maxTokens` parameter.

requirements.exclusion: A bound in the model's tokens, and the tokenizer is the model's: a validator cannot count the tokens of a result's `content` without knowing which tokenizer produced it (the result's `model` names the model, not its vocabulary), so an over-long answer cannot be shown.

source.quote: Clients SHOULD implement user approval controls

requirements.exclusion: Binds the client's user interface — what it shows the user, offers them, or lets them do — and none of that reaches the wire: a recording carries the client's messages, not its screens. The reference host this project ships has no interactive interface at all (it answers from its interaction script, `crates/mcp-reference-host/src/handler.rs`), so the clause is a host-implementation property, reviewed in the host, never judged from a trace.

source.quote: Both parties SHOULD validate message content

requirements.exclusion: Validation is internal; its outcome is whatever each party sends next, and the shape of what they send is judged directly by the clauses that constrain it (tool-message balance, message roles).

source.quote: Clients SHOULD respect model preference hints

requirements.exclusion: Hints are advisory and mapping them is the client's choice (the page: clients "MAY map hints to equivalent models from different providers"); the result's `model` names what was used, but no rule says which model a hint selects, so no answer contradicts one.

source.quote: Clients SHOULD implement rate limiting

requirements.exclusion: A request schedule: rate limiting is measured in elapsed time, which checks may not consult (LIFE-015, the time boundary in `02-architecture.md`), and its threshold is the client's own policy.

source.quote: Both parties MUST handle sensitive data appropriately

requirements.exclusion: "Appropriately" names no observable criterion, and which data is sensitive is a semantic judgement about content (see the elicitation pages' sensitive-information clauses): no message can be shown to have mishandled it.

source.quote: Servers MUST ensure that when replying to a `stopReason: "toolUse"`, each `ToolUseContent` item is responded to with a `ToolResultContent` item with a matching `toolUseId`, and that the user message contains only tool results (no other content types)
Both parties SHOULD implement iteration limits for tool loops

requirements.exclusion: A limit on a loop's length is a policy whose threshold the page does not set: any finite loop in a recording is consistent with some limit, and an unbounded one cannot be recorded.
